judged_text: Both external fetches (`open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` here and `open(url).read` in TopicEmbed.import_remote) use open-uri with no open/read timeout. A stalled or slow-loris feed/article server hangs the sidekiq thread indefinitely (open-uri has no default open timeout); with retry: false the hourly poll slot is consumed by the hung thread and repeated hangs exhaust the sidekiq worker pool, stalling unrelated background jobs on the instance.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds two external HTTP fetches via open-uri: `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` in `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` and `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` in `TopicEmbed.import_remote`. Neither call passes explicit `open_timeout`/`read_timeout` (or any other limiting options) or wraps the fetch in error handling, so a slow/stalled remote server can tie up a Sidekiq worker thread for an extended period. The finding’s broader claim about “indefinitely” depends on Ruby/open-uri defaults not shown in the diff, but the lack of explicit timeouts is a real, diff-grounded robustness concern.
